PullRequest.Title: editor: Fix Windows session home breadcrumbs
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Fix session-home breadcrumbs falling back to the full filesystem path on Windows when a resource URI and its registered home differ in drive-letter or directory casing.

- Match static and template homes case-insensitively for local files on Windows/macOS, while preserving case-sensitive matching on Linux and for non-file schemes.
- Preserve the resource's original path casing in the resolved home so breadcrumb traversal stops at the correct directory.
- Apply the same local-file comparison when discovering resumed SDK session homes from recorded artifacts, preserving the session ID's casing.
- Add regression coverage for drive paths, UNC paths, query/fragment removal, template parameters, sibling exclusion, and the exact shortened breadcrumb elements.

Follow-up to #333404 and #333435. Existing provider/session labels remain unchanged.

## Validation

- Reproduced seven new regression failures on Windows before the fix.
- `npm run gulp compile-client` - passed with zero errors.
- Targeted Windows browser tests for URI labels, breadcrumbs, and session-home providers - **50 passing**.
- Hygiene checks for all six changed files - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

cc @sandy081

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or switching to a local Windows/macOS session artifact with breadcrumbs enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: BreadcrumbsModel construction synchronously calls LabelService.getUriHome, scans registered static/template home formatters, walks the resource's parent path, and renders the shortened breadcrumb before the editor breadcrumb model is ready.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered static/template home formatters and resource path depth; effective cardinality is one scan per breadcrumb model initialization, not per breadcrumb element.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-thread execution per breadcrumb model initialization or refresh; no queue, limiter, IPC, or parallel work is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache exists before or after the change; both versions scan the same registered formatter collections. Template regular expressions remain precompiled at formatter registration, and the diff only enables case-insensitive matching for local file templates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous call path and formatter cardinality from BreadcrumbsModel._initFilePathInfo through LabelService.findHomeFormatter; high confidence that no boundary operation was added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of session-home formatter groups and editor switches varies, but realistic work remains an in-memory scan over registered homes plus path-depth traversal; the added case-insensitive comparisons do not establish a user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff preserves scan frequency and collection size, changing local-file comparisons to case-insensitive matching and preserving resource casing; any extra comparison cost is bounded string work required by the behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refreshing local agent-host resource-label homes after session or draft-session changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The in-memory session-change handler synchronously enumerates known sessions and their already-loaded artifacts, derives home URIs, groups them, and updates formatter registrations before label-home refresh completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Known sessions plus artifacts attached to copilotcli sessions, after grouping homes by parent; registration count remains one template/root formatter per effective parent group.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous refresh per emitted session/draft-session event; artifacts are processed serially in the existing loops, and formatter registrations are deduplicated by parent-group keys.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session and artifact data are already held in memory. Existing registration maps reuse formatters for unchanged group keys; the diff neither adds a cache nor invalidates one. Cold startup and warm updates retain the same session/artifact enumeration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the constructor event wiring and updateResourceLabelHomeFormatters implementation that the changed comparison and session-ID extraction remain in-memory and do not alter event frequency or fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session and artifact counts vary, but the effective cardinality remains one URI containment check per artifact and one grouping pass per refresh. There is no evidence of large enough added case-folding cost to cause measurable latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed comparator performs case-insensitive local-path containment and the direct slice replaces relativePath without increasing refresh frequency, artifact cardinality, registration churn, or boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Registering and using template-based resource label homes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Formatter registration compiles one anchored regular expression, while subsequent URI label/home requests execute that precompiled expression during synchronous label resolution.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Compatible registered template formatter count and resource path length; effective work is one anchored regex match per compatible formatter per lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Registration and matching run synchronously on the caller thread; one regex execution occurs per compatible template formatter during each label lookup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The compiled matcher remains cached in IHomeFormatterRegistration for its registration lifetime in both versions. The added ignore-case flag does not introduce recompilation per lookup or alter registration lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from createTemplateFormatterRegistration and findHomeFormatter that compilation remains one-time and matching cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact formatter counts and lookup frequency vary across workbench surfaces, but matching remains anchored and segment-bounded, with no catastrophic backtracking mechanism introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Case-insensitive local-file matching changes regex semantics but does not add repeated compilation, unbounded retention, or new scaling work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. Traced breadcrumb label resolution, template/static home matching, and local agent-session home refreshes; checked formatter lifecycle, event frequency, artifact cardinality, cache behavior, concurrency, and transitive expensive boundaries. No actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
